text:
sasha_csm: Heads-up — Clearwave (mid-market) usage fell ~45% this month. Renewal in 28 days. Thinking a short 'bridgeflow' save plan: rapid enable session, temporary discount with rollback trigger, and a feedback loop to catch product gaps.

maria_cs: Ugh, timing sucks. Are they on a dedicated deployment or hosted?

sasha_csm: Hosted. No infra blockers. Primary risk is feature confusion + churn from missed integrations.

jon_sales: I had a quick call last week — they tried the new reranking option and saw inconsistent results on their dataset. They flagged latency and quality.

ada_se: @jon_sales can you drop the convo notes? we need root-cause (prompt vs model vs config).

jon_sales: pasted notes below:
```
- Tried rerank v2 on payments dataset
- Saw 12% drop in top-1 precision vs baseline
- Increased token cost by ~18% with batching config left at defaults
- They reverted to older prompt and are throttling usage
```

noah_ops: :eyes: That suggests both quality and cost concerns — classic downgrade vector.

maria_cs: Proposed bridgeflow (very compact):
1) 1-hour enable + hands-on prompts lab (owner: sasha_csm)
2) Temporary 20% credit for 30 days if adoption drops below threshold (owner: jon_sales)
3) Eng triage to run quick A/B on rerank config + fallback policy (owner: tom_product + eng-deploy-bot)
4) Capture structured feedback and onboard them into a mini-qa loop (owner: ada_se)

sasha_csm: I'll schedule the enable session for EOW. Draft outreach template below — please tweak: 
```
Hi Team Clearwave — we've noticed some changes in the model outputs on your recent runs. Can we do a hands-on lab this week (30–60m) to walk through prompts, rerank settings, and rollback paths? We'll bring an eng rep to run a quick A/B and a config-safe fallback. If we can't get adoption back above X% in 30 days, we'll apply a temporary credit while we remediate.
```

tom_product: For the eng triage, quick plan: run a 2-arm test (current -> rerank v2 with tuned threshold), measure top-1 precision and latency at sample-size 1000. If latency > 350ms p50 or precision drops > 6pts, auto-fallback to v1. I can own the test and report.

eng-deploy-bot: scheduled test-job #9863 -> started at 1723456820, ETA 15m. Logs: https://ci.redwood/test/9863

ada_se: For feedback capture, let's use this simple tracker row we can paste into the ticket: 
```
- symptom: (quality|latency|cost|integration)
- example: short text + run id
- impact_score: (1-5)
- immediate_action: (fallback|tune|credit)
- owner: @person
- due: YYYY-MM-DD
```

sasha_csm: Nice. Who drafts the credit/offer language for legal? @jon_sales?

jon_sales: I can draft. Keep it short: "30-day 20% usage credit contingent on active remediation and attendance to enable session." I'll ping legal if needed.

maria_cs: Quick decision points: do we offer exec sync or keep with CSM+AE? My vote: start with CSM+AE; escalate exec only if enable session fails.

noah_ops: Also recommend we set a renewal-risk flag in CRM and add 'priority outreach' tag so onboarding materials are surfaced by growth.

sasha_csm: Agreed. Action items (owners + due):
- Schedule enable + send template (sasha_csm) — due 1723533189 (EOW)
- Draft credit wording (jon_sales) — due 1723490000 (48h)
- Run eng A/B and report (tom_product + eng-deploy-bot) — ETA 1723457700
- Create feedback tracker row & ticket (ada_se) — due 1723457000
- CRM risk flag + priority tag (noah_ops) — done

maria_cs: I'll join the enable to support adoption metrics and capture next-step commitments.

sasha_csm: If the A/B shows quality fixable by threshold tuning we keep them and close risk. If not, we prep downgrade path: phased capacity reduction with clear return-to-service steps and a final decision 7 days before renewal.

jon_sales: :thumbsup: I also suggest we ask for two sample runs from their integration before the enable session so eng can reproduce.

ada_se: I'll add the sample-run ask to the outreach template.

sasha_csm: Great. I'll send the invite + template now and update this thread with the enable invite and eng job outcome. Thanks all. :rocket:
